interpretation.interpretation: The diagram shows the geocentric arrangement of the seven planetary spheres around the Earth. The central brown dot labelled "TER RA" is the Earth, placed at the common centre. Around it are six more concentric circles, each carrying a small painted head with a split red label naming a planet or luminary. From the innermost sphere outward the order is: "LU NA" (Moon), "MER CUR" (Mercury), "UE NUS" (Venus, probably written "UE" or "UI" for "VENUS"), "SO L" (Sun), "MA RS" (Mars), "IO UIS" (Jupiter) and "SATU RNUS" (Saturn). This is the standard Ptolemaic or Macrobian order of the planets, with the Sun fourth, in the middle of the series. The heads are personifications of the planets, and the rays around the orange head mark the Sun's light. The diagram probably illustrates a passage on the order and distances of the planets in a computistic or natural-philosophical text, since the surrounding page is written in Latin. Reading from the top, the outermost circle is the sphere of Saturn and the innermost circle is the sphere of the Moon.
interpretation.evidence: The red labels are the Latin planet names, and each is split around a head placed on a circle. The Earth label is at the centre. The order of the labels from the centre outward, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Sun, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, matches the geocentric planetary order. The heads in a single vertical column and the rayed orange head for the Sun are visible features that support this reading. The Step 1 reading "UE NUS" for the Venus label is uncertain, because the second letter is unclear and may be "I", giving "UI NUS". Step 1 also lists the Earth circle as the seventh circle, but the central dot has no circle of its own, so the label "seventh circle" is the innermost ring, which is the lunar sphere. The attribution to a specific source text is not certain and is not named.
